reading.body:
Meta's Sarpy County campus has no published power capacity figure, so its size relative to other US data center infrastructure cannot be determined from operator specifications. The campus sits in Nebraska, a state where 21 data center facilities are mapped but none publish power specifications to this site, making Sarpy the only facility in the state with any rank at all by that metric. Meta reports $2.5 billion in cumulative investment and ground breaking in 2017, indicating long-term commitment to the site.

The facility operates buildings certified to LEED Gold standard. Meta states that electricity consumption is matched with 100 percent renewable energy as part of global net-zero operations, and that a Meta-supported project is adding 320 megawatts of new renewable energy capacity in Nebraska. These figures describe energy sourcing policy rather than the campus's own load or its contribution to state grid demand.

Without published megawatt figures, assessing whether this campus materially affects AI scaling constraints requires inference from investment scale and timeline alone. The $2.5 billion commitment and 2017 start date place it among Meta's major infrastructure plays, but the absence of any published capacity specification from Meta itself means this site cannot quantify its role in either the company's current AI training footprint or Nebraska's grid planning.
